title: Pad Thai
subtitle: Thai stir-fried rice noodles with egg, prawns, and peanuts
excerpt: Thailand's most famous noodle dish: flat rice noodles stir-fried over blistering heat with eggs, prawns, and bean sprouts in a sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar, scattered with crushed peanuts and spring onion.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad thai was promoted as a national dish of Thailand in the 1930s and 1940s by Prime Minister Plaek Phibunsongkhram as part of a nation-building campaign that encouraged rice consumption and reduced wheat noodle use. The dish became ubiquitous at street stalls and is now the most recognisable Thai export dish worldwide. The defining flavour is tamarind: the paste provides sourness and depth that cannot be replicated with vinegar or lime. The technique requires very high heat; domestic hobs rarely reach wok temperatures, so the dish should be cooked in very small batches. The eggs are pushed to the side and scrambled directly in the pan before being folded through the noodles.

content.text: Soak the noodles in cold water only (not boiling water) for 30 minutes before cooking. They should be pliable but still firm; they will finish cooking in the wok. Cook in the smallest possible batches: crowding the wok makes the noodles steam instead of fry and the result is sticky and wet.

items.preparation: flat rice noodles; soaked in cold water for 30 minutes and drained

content.text: Mix the fish sauce, soy sauce, and sugar together in a small bowl. Set aside. Heat a wok or large frying pan over the highest possible heat until smoking.

Add the oil, then the shallot and garlic. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the prawns and cook for 1 minute until just pink. Add the soaked noodles and the sauce mixture. Toss everything together for 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and cooked through.

Push the noodles to one side. Crack the eggs into the empty space. Scramble briefly, then fold through the noodles before fully set. Add the bean sprouts and spring onion. Toss for 30 seconds. Serve scattered with peanuts and chilli flakes with lime wedges on the side.
